tour.heading: Six tools, one goal
tour.intro: Each part of the toolkit does one job. Here is what each tool looks like, what it is for, and when to reach for it.

tools.title: Treatment Planning Tool
tools.tagline: Create your treatment plan by identifying and mapping the suicide risk and protective factors for your client, selecting interventions that target those factors, and building out a three-phase treatment plan.
tools.useWhen: In sessions 1–4, then revisit as things change

tools.title: Make A Safety Plan
tools.tagline: Build a Stanley-Brown safety plan step by step with your client, then print a copy for them to keep.
tools.useWhen: Early in treatment, and whenever risk changes

tools.title: Treatment Library
tools.tagline: Search vetted assessments, worksheets, handouts and evidence-based practices for youth, families and schools.
tools.useWhen: When planning a session or a family meeting

tools.title: Community Resources
tools.tagline: Find referrals near your client for ongoing care after their time with Rise ends.
tools.useWhen: When linking your client to their next step in care

tools.title: Navigating Schools
tools.tagline: Tips for working with schools, a school partner interview guide, your client's school card, and a contact card to give schools.
tools.useWhen: Before your first visit to a new school

tools.title: Self-Care & Support
tools.tagline: Grounding practices, a wall of wins, peer support and consultation, for you.
tools.useWhen: Any time, not just when things feel hard

journey.heading: Your toolkit across a Rise treatment
journey.intro: The toolkit follows the three phases of Rise's short-term model. Here is which tools do the most work in each phase.

phases.note: Assess risk, build the safety plan together, and map what is driving the client's suicidal ideation.
Choose evidence-based interventions for the top factors and practice skills in session.
Re-screen, revisit the safety plan, and link the client to their next step in care.

whySummary.heading: Built to close real gaps in care

goal.heading: 1. What Is the Goal of This Toolkit?
paragraphs: The goal of this toolkit is to reduce suicidal ideation among youth served through the Rise short-term treatment model. It does this by supporting the therapists who work with them: consolidating practical, evidence-informed tools in one place and by providing resources, tips and strategies to make your day-to-day practice easier, more efficient, and more connected.

Rather than replacing clinical judgment or training, it's meant to give therapists a clear roadmap, vetted resources, guidance for working with schools, and support for their own sustainability in this rewarding, yet challenging, work.

how.heading: 3. How Was This Toolkit Developed?
how.intro: We listened to your experiences and collaboratively designed solutions to address your needs. We used a framework called the Discover, Design, Build, Test model.

pairs.solution: We know 12 sessions is short. That's why we built this toolkit. Developed with therapists, clinical and research experts in youth suicide prevention, the Treatment Roadmap structures our brief model around what matters most in a short window: reducing risk and stabilizing crisis, building emotion regulation, problem-solving and support seeking skills, and building a life worth living, all in service of reducing suicidal ideation.

pairs.concern: We spend too much time looking for resources.
pairs.solution: We have created a vetted Treatment Library for you to pull from. Search for exactly what you need to help clients link to resources in the community, referrals for therapy after your treatment wraps, and access a library of evidence-based worksheets and tools to use in therapy with youth, families and schools.

pairs.concern: Working in the schools is complicated.
pairs.solution: We have built a school navigation page filled with resources to support your work in schools. We have a list of questions for you to ask schools to get to know the lay of the land, we have tips for navigating tricky interactions, and suggestions for collaborating with schools to best support youth and families.

pairs.concern: This work takes a personal toll.
pairs.solution: Working with youth at risk for suicide is some of the hardest clinical work there is. These tools help you spot burnout early, build resilience into your practice, provide you with tips and tricks for your peers, and allow you to schedule a consultation call with our licensed clinical psychologist.

items.title: Treatment Roadmap
items.body: Your guide through the clinical process: starting with risk assessment and safety planning, skill building and practice, consolidation and transition planning.

items.title: Treatment Library
items.body: Your one-stop-shop for therapy resources. From vetted community resources to suggested referrals, browse recommended clinical assessment tools, youth and family handouts, intervention worksheets, and more.

items.title: Navigating Schools
items.body: Your tips and tricks for navigating the complexity of schools. Learn what questions to ask to get the information you need, how to clarify roles and responsibilities, and how to coordinate with school teams.

items.title: Therapist Self-Care
items.body: Your reminder to care for yourself. Strategies for managing vicarious trauma and compassion fatigue, recognizing signs and developing action plans to address burnout, and connecting with your peers.

useIt.heading: 5. How Do I Use This Toolkit?
useIt.intro: This toolkit is designed to be flexible: use what works for you, your clients and your workflow. Here are some suggestions:

guidance.title: Start with the Treatment Roadmap.
guidance.body: Use it to help you plan and deliver your therapy. Revisit session by session to see where you are and what comes next.

guidance.title: Dip into the Treatment Library when you need something specific.
guidance.body: Align it with the Roadmap, and treat it like a search tool: pull a handout for a family session, grab an assessment before intake, or find a referral when treatment is wrapping up.

guidance.title: Turn to Navigating Schools before or during any school-facing work.
guidance.body: Review the sample questions ahead of a school meeting, or reference the role-clarification tips when a case starts to feel tangled between systems.

guidance.title: Revisit Therapist Self-Care regularly, not just when things feel hard.
guidance.body: Build a check-in by integrating these tools into your own routine - weekly, monthly, whatever's sustainable - so you catch signs of strain early rather than after burnout sets in.

tips: You don't need to use every tool with every client. Pick what's relevant to the case in front of you.
Tools can be adapted. Use your clinical judgment to fit language, pacing, and content to each youth and family.
Come back often. This is meant to be a living resource you return to throughout a case, not a one-time read!
If you want support, or to talk through a case, remember you can also schedule a consultation call with our licensed clinical psychologist.

closing.pre: If you have suggestions to improve our toolkit, please let us know!
closing.post: The goal is to support you best – we need your help knowing how to do this!
